request: Amine-functionalized sorbent for direct air capture (DAC) from atmospheric CO₂ (410 ppm). The material combines mesoporous silica with polyethylenimine (PEI) and polyethylene glycol (PEG) additives. Operational targets: (1) CO₂ capture capacity >3 mol CO₂/kg sorbent at standard air, (2) fast kinetics for low humidity operation, (3) regeneration at 80-100°C requiring <1.5 MJ/kg energy, and (4) 1000+ cycle stability.

Carbon capture sorbent for flue gas application (5-15% CO₂ from coal power plant). The material uses activated carbon impregnated with alkali metal oxides (K2CO3, Na2CO3) for CO₂ chemisorption. Specifications: (1) achieve 90% CO₂/N₂ selectivity at 60°C and 1 bar, (2) fast breakthrough (10 min at 5 L/min), (3) thermal regeneration at 150-200°C with >95% capacity recovery, and (4) durability for 500+ cycles.

Moisture-stable carbon dioxide capture material for humid environments. The sorbent combines zeolite with moisture-blocking polymer coating and amine functionality. Design requirements: (1) maintain >2 mol CO₂/kg capacity in 60% relative humidity, (2) avoid amine hydrolysis and loss, (3) regenerate with swing temperature (60-100°C), and (4) perform effectively for equipment deployment in coastal/tropical regions.

Pressure swing adsorption (PSA) sorbent for point-source CO₂ capture at industrial facilities (cement, steel, ammonia plants). The adsorbent combines hierarchical porous carbon with polyamine for rapid cycling: (1) 5-min adsorption at 10 bar CO₂, (2) 5-min regeneration at 1 bar (vacuum-assisted), (3) >95 wt% recovery, and (4) stable performance over 5000+ cycles.

Post-combustion carbon capture sorbent for retrofitting existing fossil fuel power plants. The material captures 90% of flue gas CO₂ (5-8% CO₂, 70-100°C, 1 bar). Design uses pelletized activated carbon with K2CO3/NaOH impregnation in moving bed reactors. Regeneration targets: (1) thermal swing 150-180°C, (2) <3 MJ/kg energy demand, and (3) maintain capacity through 500+ cycles.

Metal-organic framework (MOF) for CO₂ capture with high selectivity over N₂. The framework combines zinc ions with organic linkers optimized for CO₂ binding. Specifications: (1) >50 mol CO₂/kg capacity at 1 bar and 25°C, (2) CO₂/N₂ selectivity >100, (3) rapid adsorption (breakthrough <5 min), (4) regeneration at 60°C vacuum, and (5) long-term stability >1000 cycles.

Temperature-swing adsorption sorbent for continuous CO₂ removal from industrial exhaust. The material uses amine-impregnated resin with optimized thermal swing between 50°C (adsorption) and 120°C (regeneration). Performance criteria: (1) CO₂ capacity 2-3 mol/kg, (2) fast kinetics for 30-min cycles, (3) minimal energy demand for regeneration, and (4) no chemical loss over 2000+ cycles.

Modular CO₂ capture cartridge for retrofit applications in HVAC systems of large buildings. Each cartridge treats 1000-2000 CFM of indoor air to maintain <500 ppm CO₂ (comfort standard). Design combines granular amine sorbent with moisture desiccant layer. Service life: 1-2 years before regeneration, with field-level changeout procedure.
